answer.answer: The National Bamboo Mission (NBM) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2018-19 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare [E01]. It was restructured after a 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act that excluded bamboo from the definition of tree, allowing bamboo grown in non-forest areas to be outside forest regulations [E01]. During 2022-23, the NBM was merged with the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) scheme [E01]. The mission focuses on developing the complete value chain of the bamboo sector, from planting material and plantation to processing, marketing, and brand building in a cluster approach [E01]. It is currently implemented in 24 States/UTs [E01]. Key objectives include increasing bamboo plantation area on non-forest lands to supplement farm income and support climate resilience, improving post-harvest management, promoting product development, rejuvenating the bamboo industry, promoting skill development, and reducing dependency on bamboo imports [E01]. The scheme provides benefits including assistance for bamboo nursery establishment, cultivation, post-harvest processing, product manufacturing, capacity building, and entrepreneurship [E02].
